narrative.title: Merging Two Ledger Chains Digit by Digit
narrative.scenario: Two accounting terminals store big balances as digit chains, least significant digit first — the one layout where addition can start immediately at the head. A reconciliation pass walks both chains together, sums paired digits plus the running carry, emits each sum digit, and appends one final digit if a carry outlasts both chains.
narrative.inputFormat: Two arrays nums1 and nums2 of digits 0-9, each representing a non-negative integer with the least significant digit first.
narrative.outputFormat: The digit sequence of the sum, least significant digit first.

testCases.explanation: 342 + 465 = 807, emitted least significant digit first as 7, 0, 8.
0 + 0 = 0 — a single zero digit, no carry anywhere.

hintLevels: Level 1: Digits arrive backwards on purpose — the least significant digit leads, which is exactly where addition begins.
Level 2: March both chains at once: sum the paired digits plus carry, emit sum % 10, carry sum / 10; treat a finished chain as a stream of zeros.
Level 3: The loop must run until both chains are dry AND the carry is spent — a final 1 node after the longer chain is the classic miss.
